title: The clouds (12.5, D170): which cloud patterns can show per season and cloud level, the season's palette over them, and the weather descriptions that name a sky. The patterns are drawn as code in src/scene/clouds.js (CLOUD_PATTERNS).

patterns.description: Pattern ids from src/scene/clouds.js, such as heap-a. A full-sky pattern (sheet, rain, storm, fog) is the backdrop; the others are scattered over the sky (or over that backdrop) until they cover the level's `cover`.

levels.description: Per cloud level, 0 clear to 5 black (rules/weather-scales.json): `cover`, how much of the sky the clouds fill (should agree with rules/moon.json's cloudCover); `veil`, how much of the sun, the moon and the stars shows between or through them; `glints`, how many of the water's glints still flick; `sunHides`, how much of the time a cloud is over the sun when the sun is off the picture (on it, the clouds drawn decide); `dusk`, how much of the night tint the clouds bring.

seasons.description: Per season (an id from content/weather/): the palette the patterns are drawn in, and per cloud level (0 to 5) the patterns that can show.

palette.description: White clouds go light, cloud, shade, dark; grey ones cloud, shade, sheet, sheetDark; storm ones sheet, sheetDark, storm, stormDark.

wet.description: Rain cloud: at cloud `level` with precipitation at `precipitation` or more, these patterns show in place of the season's.

fog.description: A weather tagged fog hides the sky whatever the cloud level: the first entry whose min..max holds the level gives the patterns, and `veil`, how much of the sun shows through.

descriptions.description: Weather descriptions that name a sky, by string key (weather.<season>.weathers.<n>.descriptions.<n>): their own patterns over the table, the cloud levels they suit (a test wants every level the weather can roll), and optionally `drift` (how fast, times the wind's), `low` (kept near the horizon) and `sunHides` (in place of the level's).
